title: Ministry of Jal Shakti Releases Policy on Data Sharing, Interoperability and Stakeholder Access under Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure
body_text:
Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, issued the Policy on Data Sharing, Interoperability and Stakeholder Access under Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) today, establishing a secure, federated, interoperable and accountable framework for sharing and governing rural drinking water data across States, Union Territories, local governance institutions and approved sectoral stakeholders.
The Policy marks an important milestone in the evolution of India's rural drinking water sector from infrastructure creation to assured, accountable and service-oriented drinking water delivery. It provides a comprehensive framework to support infrastructure lifecycle management, source sustainability, service assurance, citizen-centric accountability and evidence-based decision-making.  It also establishes governance principles for data sharing, interoperability and stakeholder access within the Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure. It promotes the use of common identifiers, standardised metadata, interoperable registries and secure digital services to enable seamless exchange of information while preserving institutional accountability, privacy and cybersecurity.
Key objective of this Policy is to enable governed and interoperable data exchange between DDWS, State/UTs, Gram Panchayats, Government organisations and authorised sectoral stakeholders. The framework strengthens Panchayat-centric governance, citizen participation, grievance redressal, participatory asset monitoring and service accountability across the rural water ecosystem. Through approved and purpose-based access mechanisms, stakeholders may develop innovative solutions relating to operation and maintenance, water-quality monitoring, infrastructure management, predictive maintenance, geospatial planning, Digital Twins, Artificial Intelligence-enabled analytics and decision-support systems.
Recognising the importance of trust in digital ecosystems, the Policy incorporates robust provisions relating to privacy, personal data protection, cybersecurity, data classification, access governance and public-interest safeguards. It adopts a tiered data-access framework to ensure secure, responsible and purpose-limited use of information while protecting sensitive infrastructure and personal data.
The Policy further positions Sujalam Bharat as a long-term public digital infrastructure for rural water utility governance, supporting transparency, innovation, operational efficiency and sustainable service delivery.  With the release of this Policy, the department takes a significant step towards building a trusted digital foundation for rural drinking water governance and strengthening the delivery of reliable, sustainable and accountable water services for rural communities across the country.

enrichment.summary: The Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti, released a Policy on Data Sharing, Interoperability and Stakeholder Access under the Sujalam Bharat Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) on 20 August 2026. The policy creates a secure, federated and interoperable framework for sharing rural drinking water data among the Centre, States/UTs, Gram Panchayats and approved sectoral stakeholders, using common identifiers, standardised metadata and interoperable registries. It incorporates tiered, purpose-based data access along with privacy, cybersecurity and public-interest safeguards to support Panchayat-centric governance, citizen accountability and AI/geospatial-enabled service delivery in the rural water sector.
enrichment.context:
Sujalam Bharat is envisioned as the digital public infrastructure (DPI) layer supporting India's rural drinking water governance, building on the data and asset information generated under the Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), which since 2019 has aimed to provide functional household tap connections (FHTC) to every rural home. As JJM approaches saturation of physical infrastructure, the policy focus is shifting from 'infrastructure creation' to 'service assurance'—ensuring water quality, source sustainability, and long-term operation and maintenance (O&M) of assets, which now requires robust, shareable data systems across Gram Panchayats, State Water and Sanitation Missions, and the Centre.

This initiative fits into India's broader DPI strategy (modelled on Aadhaar, UPI, and other 'digital stack' approaches) of using common identifiers, open APIs, and federated data architecture to enable innovation by third-party stakeholders while retaining institutional control and privacy safeguards. For rural water governance, such interoperability is expected to support predictive maintenance, water-quality monitoring, geospatial planning, and AI-enabled decision-support tools, while strengthening grievance redressal and citizen participation at the Panchayat level, consistent with the government's push for evidence-based, decentralized service delivery in flagship missions.

prelims_questions.question: The 'Sujalam Bharat' Digital Public Infrastructure, for which a data-sharing and interoperability policy was released in 2026, is primarily associated with which sector?
prelims_questions.explanation: Sujalam Bharat DPI, under the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation, is a digital infrastructure for governing rural drinking water data linked to the Jal Jeevan Mission ecosystem.

prelims_questions.question: Which of the following best describes the approach adopted by the Ministry of Jal Shakti's Policy on Data Sharing under Sujalam Bharat?
options: Complete open access to all data for any citizen without restriction
A tiered, purpose-based data access framework with privacy and cybersecurity safeguards
Centralisation of all data exclusively with the Union Government, excluding States
Mandatory private sector ownership of all rural water infrastructure data
prelims_questions.explanation: The policy adopts a tiered data-access framework ensuring secure, responsible and purpose-limited use of data, incorporating privacy, cybersecurity and public-interest safeguards.

mains_questions.question: Discuss the significance of Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) in strengthening service delivery under rural drinking water schemes in India, with reference to the Sujalam Bharat data-sharing policy.
Examine how interoperable data systems and AI-enabled analytics can improve infrastructure sustainability and accountability in India's rural water sector.

study_notes.reason: The release both introduces a discrete, nameable policy and DPI (testable facts: name, parent department, mechanism) and carries genuine analytical weight as a case of India's DPI strategy being extended to sectoral, federal rural water governance and the shift from infrastructure creation to service assurance.

prelims.point: Sujalam Bharat is the Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) for rural drinking water governance, launched by the Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation (DDWS), Ministry of Jal Shakti (policy released 20 August 2026).
prelims.why_important: A newly named DPI initiative under a specific ministry/department is a classic 'match the scheme to the ministry' prelims item.

prelims.point: Jal Jeevan Mission (JJM), launched 2019, aims to provide Functional Household Tap Connections (FHTC) to every rural household; Sujalam Bharat builds on JJM's data and asset base.
prelims.why_important: Distinguishes JJM (infrastructure mission) from Sujalam Bharat (the digital data layer built on top of it), a distinction UPSC favours testing.

prelims.point: The policy adopts a tiered, purpose-based data-access framework using common identifiers, standardised metadata and interoperable registries for data sharing among Centre, States/UTs, Gram Panchayats and approved stakeholders.
prelims.why_important: Tests understanding of DPI design principles (federated architecture, tiered access) as applied to a specific sector.

mains.point: The policy signals a structural shift in rural water governance from 'infrastructure creation' to 'service assurance' — focusing on water quality, source sustainability and O&M as JJM approaches physical saturation.
mains.theme: Evolution of flagship missions from creation to sustainability
mains.analytical_use: Useful for questions on how welfare schemes must evolve post-saturation of physical targets to ensure long-term service delivery.

mains.point: Sujalam Bharat extends India's DPI model (akin to Aadhaar/UPI) into a sector-specific, federated data architecture spanning Centre, States and Gram Panchayats.
mains.theme: Digital Public Infrastructure as a governance tool
mains.analytical_use: Deployable in questions on how DPI principles (interoperability, open APIs, institutional control) can be replicated across sectors beyond finance/identity.

mains.point: The framework strengthens Panchayat-centric governance, citizen participation, grievance redressal and participatory asset monitoring in rural water service delivery.
mains.analytical_use: Supports answers on strengthening the third tier of governance through digital tools and data ownership at the Panchayat level.

mains.point: Enabling AI-driven analytics, predictive maintenance, geospatial planning and Digital Twins for water infrastructure through governed stakeholder data access.
mains.analytical_use: Illustrative example for questions on leveraging AI/geospatial tools for infrastructure management and predictive governance.

mains.point: The policy embeds privacy, personal data protection, cybersecurity and data-classification safeguards to balance innovation with institutional accountability and public interest.
mains.theme: Data governance and privacy in digital public infrastructure
mains.analytical_use: Relevant for questions on balancing data-sharing innovation with citizen privacy and cybersecurity risks in sectoral DPIs.

both.concept: Sujalam Bharat as a sector-specific Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) layered on Jal Jeevan Mission data.
both.prelims_angle: Identify the correct nodal department (DDWS, Ministry of Jal Shakti), its relationship to JJM, and its core design features (federated, interoperable, tiered access).
both.mains_angle: Analyse how DPI principles are being extended from national identity/payment systems to sector-specific rural governance, and what this implies for federal data-sharing, decentralisation and service assurance beyond infrastructure creation.

low_priority.point: Generic laudatory language describing the policy as a 'trusted digital foundation' and 'significant step' for rural water governance.
low_priority.reason: Promotional framing without specific, testable or analytically distinct content.
Purely administrative detail with no exam relevance.
